facts.text: Estral Beach got its name from the Spanish word for "star," reflecting early settlers' admiration for the night sky.
The village officially became incorporated in 1925, marking its transition from a small lakeside community to an incorporated municipality.
Estral Beach sits on Lake Erie's northwest shore at Swan Creek's mouth, about eight miles south of the Detroit River's mouth.
The Strong Unit of the Detroit River International Wildlife Refuge lies within Estral Beach's northern edge, offering protected wetlands for wildlife.
Only two miles southwest of Estral Beach stands the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station, a key power source for the region.
Estral Beach is part of Berlin Charter Township in northeastern Monroe County, placing it within the township's administrative boundaries.
